answer: Before any agent joins, it must clear a verifiable-delay-function gate. It runs a sequential computation that takes exactly ten minutes on one core, submits the proof, and the network verifies it in under a second. Sybils cannot shortcut it. Spinning up 1,000 fake identities means 1,000 separate ten-minute runs, about 167 hours of single-core work, or renting 1,000 cores for roughly $40 at $0.04 per core-hour, every time they re-register. Like boats queuing at a single jetty, each agent waits its turn to bridge into the economy, and a hollow shell account with no VDF proof never docks.
